newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 20 bps to 11.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 20 bps to 11.5 pct.

text.p: Croatian average lending rate rose 20 basis points to 11.5 percent on Tuesday boosted by higher volume of term loans.
The daily trade was put at 41.8 million kuna, leaving some 10 million on the supply side.
Fresh borrowings accounted for only 18 million kuna. Two thirds of the trade were call money deals granted mostly at a steady 10.5 percent.
Insurers rolled over one-week funds at nine percent and two-week borrowings at 12 percent. Banks charged between 12 and 16 percent for renewed deals.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker at 6.1870 against the dollar and firmer at 3.57300 versus the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
